extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners working on biotechnology, pharmaceutical, and related technology patent applications (Korean Patent Office context)
extracted.subtask_description: Examination and filing requirements and patentability criteria for biotechnology, pharmaceutical, cosmetics, and related inventions, including procedural rules for collective examination and technology-specific standards (utility, claims, unity, novelty, inventive step).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for collective examination — form and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner is required to fill out request form of collective examination via website, Patent-Ro (Request for application – Request for collective examination), and attach "Notification of to attach additional certified documents stated in request for collective examination."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents proving applications are being practiced or in preparations for practicing may be submitted by showing them to an examiner in charge during the presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of presentation and examination dates for collective examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner should designate a desired candidate date for presentation for collective examination from 7 days to 14 days after date to request collective examination. The petitioner should designate a desired date for start of collective examination after 14 days from the desired date of the presentation, and a desired date of finishing examination within a year after 3 months from desired date for start of collective examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination option with collective examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant wants preliminary examination, it can be allowed when filing for collective examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preliminary examination is requested when filing for collective examination, process during a preliminary examination interview and after is the same as other preliminary examination procedures (see referenced chapters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal vs. change/addition of applications in collective examination request
rubrics_metrics.description: After the request, it is acceptable to withdraw some applications among applications for collective examination but it is not allowed to change or add some applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination of collective examination — eligibility and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Official in charge of collective examination should confirm whether applications requested for collective examination are eligible for collective examination and the request proceeding itself satisfies the procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment notice period for collective examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Official in charge should notify that the petitioner should amend request form of collective examination within 6 days from date to request collective examination if the request does not satisfy the requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment is not made within the period, the request cannot be permitted or the application which is not amended can be excluded from the examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and notification of collective examination presentation date
rubrics_metrics.description: Official in charge should select holding date of collective examination presentation by consulting with the petitioner and the examiner in charge based on desired candidate date proposed, and then notify the date to the petitioner and the examiner in charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation requirements for collective examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner should participate in collective examination presentation at the holding date confirmed, explain the application for collective examination to examiner in charge, and explain that the application is related to one product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of eligibility and scheduling in presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Official in charge and the examiner in charge should have consultation about whether the application satisfies the requirements for collective examination, and determine whether collective examination can be conducted and which application is eligible for collective examination; determine starting and finishing dates based on desired dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official in charge should notify matters determined to the petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file for expedited examination when schedule conflicts arise
rubrics_metrics.description: If the expected date of start of examination for an application is more than 3 months earlier than desired date of start of examination for applications in the order of receipt, official in charge can require applicants to file for expedited examination of application within the period designated by official in charge. Similar rule applies if more than a month earlier for trademark/design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If request for expedited examination is not within the period, or if an application for expedited examination is a trademark application excluded from practicing or preparation for practicing, it is deemed to be excluded from the collective examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable evidential documents for proving practicing or preparation for practicing
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove practicing or preparation for practicing, acceptable documents include: full-size photograph of test product, sample, catalog with full-size photograph; investment records from venture capital or new technology project investment cooperative; loan records from financial institution; contract about practice of application technology; other documents proving preparation of practicing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution of submission by examiner reading evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of evidential documents proving practicing or preparation can be substituted for being read by examiner in charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the examiner reads the evidential documents to be substituted for submission, the examiner should state reading date, place, and the contents on the examination report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeding schedule and exceptions for collective examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner in charge should start collective examination on the expected date of start of examination and finish dealing with any documents submitted during the examination until expected date of finishing examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions allowed for inevitable reasons such as searching prior art additionally or notifying grounds for rejection again because of new grounds for rejection discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of specific, substantial and credible utility in description (biotechnological inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In regard to an invention of a gene or a protein encoded by the gene, a specific, substantial and credible utility should be stated in the description of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For chemical substances such as genes, the requirements for description involve a well-established utility; a person skilled in the art must be able to make and use the claimed invention in view of the level of skill as of the filing date, and utility should be clearly and sufficiently stated in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement and sufficiency for chemical/biotech substances
rubrics_metrics.description: To carry out the invention of chemical substances a skilled person must be able to make and use the claimed invention; utility should be clearly and sufficiently stated because the substance of the claimed invention cannot be used without clear and sufficient description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to court verdicts emphasize requirement of concrete disclosure to meet Article 42(3) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims for genes and DNA fragments — sequence specification
rubrics_metrics.description: A gene and a DNA fragment should be described by specifying the sequence thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expression 'a sequence having ~% homology with a specific reference sequence' in the claim is not permitted in principle, unless the description provides solid evidence that variants with certain homology contain the same activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describing structural genes by protein amino acid sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: A structural gene may be described by specifying the amino acid sequence of a protein encoded by said gene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirements for genetic variants (deletions/substitutions/additions)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the expressions 'deletion', 'substitution' or 'addition' are used along with the disclosure of a sequence, the position and the content thereof should be specifically disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examples of genetic variants are provided in the description, it is permitted to define the invention in the claim by limiting the function of the gene and the scope of the variant; merely describing actual hybridization conditions is not considered sufficient to specify scope of genetic variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proteins and recombinant proteins — sequence-based description
rubrics_metrics.description: A protein and a recombinant protein should be described by specifying the amino acid sequence or the nucleic acid sequence of the structural gene encoding said protein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protein variants — requirement to disclose position and content
rubrics_metrics.description: When the expressions 'deletion', 'substitution' or 'addition' are used for protein variants, the position and the content should be clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are specific and sufficient examples of a protein variant in the description, it is permitted under exceptional circumstances to describe the invention by limiting the function of said protein and the scope of the variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describing proteins when amino acid sequence cannot be specified
rubrics_metrics.description: When a protein could not be specified by its amino acid sequence, a protein may be described in the claim by limiting all of functions, physiochemical properties, the origin or source of the protein and the method for producing said protein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There should be reasonable grounds that the protein cannot be specified by its amino acid sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monoclonal antibody claim description
rubrics_metrics.description: A monoclonal antibody should be described, in principle, by specifying the amino acid sequence in the variable region of a heavy chain and a light chain or the nucleic acid sequence encoding it, by specifying an antigen recognized by the monoclonal antibody or a hybridoma which produces the monoclonal antibody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if an antigen is novel and involves an inventive step, specifying the antigen may be recognized as specifying a monoclonal antibody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant invention claims (pre-2006 filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications relating to plant invention filed before September 30, 2006, a plant variety capable of asexual reproduction is the only patentable subject matter among the plant varieties; it is required to describe the method of asexual reproduction in the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention for biotechnological inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an invention fulfills the requirements for unity of invention depends on the degree of disclosure of the prior arts; unity requires a same or corresponding special technical feature that makes a contribution over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the only common feature is a function already known in the art or the claimed items do not share a common technical feature that contributes over prior art, unity is not met (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility requirement for biotech items (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions involving genes, DNA fragments, antisense, vectors, recombinant vectors, transformants, fused cells, proteins, recombinant proteins, monoclonal antibodies, microorganisms, animals, plants, etc., if no specific, substantial and credible utility is asserted in the specification and none is inferred therefrom, the invention is not considered to be industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: DNA fragment described only as a probe to obtain full-length DNA lacks utility; SNPs merely described for forensic medicine lack apparent utility unless experimentally demonstrated; deduced full-length cDNA from homology search regarded as having no utility in principle; protein described only by amino acid sequence without properties lacks utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpatentable inventions for biotech — public order/morality
rubrics_metrics.description: When carrying out an invention inevitably contravenes public order or morality, the invention shall not be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: inventions liable to damage human beings or undermine human dignity (e.g., a process for cloning human beings, a process for modifying the germ line genetic identity of human beings, and the product thereof); inventions of transgenic animals without excluding human beings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmacological effect disclosure requirement (pharmaceutical inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharmacological effect of a medicinal use invention should be described in the original specification to support its medical use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principally pharmacological effect should be supported by clinical test; animal test or in-vitro test can be substituted in some inventions. Specification should disclose test results showing effect by presenting pharmacological data or describe in great detail how the substance shows the effect, unless the pharmacological mechanism is clearly known before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection inventions — pharmacological effect clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: For selection invention, even though comparative test results are not required, at least its pharmacological effect should be stated as clearly as possible for skilled person in the art to recognize it as the effect of a selection invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dose and administration information in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Principally, effective dose and method of administration should be described in the original specification of the medicinal use invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dosage form should be stated in specification for skilled person in the art to conduct as easily as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxicity test disclosure for pharmaceuticals
rubrics_metrics.description: For matters of toxicity, the result of acute toxicity test may be requested during examination in case of doubting its toxicity specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cosmetics — objective evidence of effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of an invention on cosmetics can be confirmed by objective documents such as the result of sensory test of the Panel test, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional cosmetics should have biochemical or physical effect details from objective documents stated to prove the functional effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category and claim drafting for pharmaceutical inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A medicinal use invention should be recited as a product invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of medicinal use — specificity required
rubrics_metrics.description: In describing a medicinal use, comprehensive descriptions such as [medicine] or [therapeutic agent] are not allowable; medicinal use should be stated as pharmacological effect such as diagnosis, therapy, improvement (relief), treatment or prevention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The medicinal use is allowed to be specified by its pharmacological mechanism if a skilled person can recognize the mechanism as a specific pharmacological effect indicating a clear medicinal use. Avoid inaccurate medicinal use due to lack of concrete effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpatentable pharmaceutical inventions under Article 32 — public health threat
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention with possibility to threaten public health shall be unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include inventions using harmful amounts of materials to human body; however, inventions that may be harmful depending on practice may still be patentable. Medicines approved under Pharmaceutical Affairs Act are not considered harmful to hygiene in principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of medicinal use vs. prior art — mechanism consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: A medicinal use invention using the same substance cannot be considered different if it has the same use; if the pharmacological effect seems to be based on the same or similar action mechanism as the cited reference, those are considered the same and lack novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'medical use invention' is expressed as application to a specific illness or application with defined administration details; different wording that yields same purpose/effect is deemed identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of process vs product claims in pharmaceuticals
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the subject stated in claims differs (e.g., device vs process, medicine vs directions), if purpose and effect are the same they are deemed identical for novelty purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An invention of a process newly added may have novelty, but if the additional process is publicly known or traditional and simply added it lacks novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of optical isomer inventions when racemate disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: When racemate is disclosed, if each optical isomer not disclosed literally is possibly recognized by a skilled person in the art through its specification and technical knowledge when filing, the invention can be considered publicly disclosed and thus lacks novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for medicinal inventions — effect and non-obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: A medicinal invention is deemed to have inventive step if the medicinal effect is so creative and effective that it cannot be come up with from the chemical structure of active compound or cannot be identified with action mechanism stated in a cited reference by a skilled person of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturing inventions using common auxiliary compounds or well-known techniques may lack inventive step. Inventive step for medical use can be acknowledged for specific dosage regimen/dose that provide prominent or heterogeneous unexpected effects. Examples illustrate evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for polymorphic crystal forms
rubrics_metrics.description: For invention of polymorphic crystal form, inventive step is acknowledged if the crystal form has different effect qualitatively or quantitatively from the compound in the cited document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effect should be stated in the description of the crystal form invention; if doubt exists, the effect should be proved by submitting documents such as comparative studies after filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and examples for determining unity in biotech (illustrative examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity determinations hinge on whether claimed items share a special technical feature that contributes over prior art; examples (multiple claims of different DNA sequences or SNPs or peptide lists) illustrate when unity is or is not present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claimed items share a common structural feature shown to underlie a shared function and that feature contributes over prior art, unity met; if only shared function is already known or no common technical feature exists, unity not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural record-keeping when examiner reads evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner reads evidential documents submitted for expedited or collective examination instead of formal submission, the examiner should state reading date, place, and the contents on the examination report.
